articles.title: Smile at Last review – photo-love-story style parable of a teen abandoned at a tough Soviet youth facility
articles.summary: With handheld camerawork, this unsentimental rite of passage film follows Mari, who tries to escape from a residential home in Estonia. This intriguing 1985 film from Estonia uses nonprofessionals and handheld camerawork, which brings faces looming up to the screen.
body: It is at one level a kind of coming-of-age story, but entirely without that genre’s usual, sentimental sense of something finally learned or gained from an emotional rite of passage – something finally to smile about, in fact. Actually, it is more of a mysterious parable, couched in the language of soap opera or photo-love story, depicting the Soviet state and its gruesome pretension to be caring or nurturing.

There is a dreamlike quality to the action, despite its ostensible kitchen-sink realism. It is almost a kind of pastoral: the young people in this institution apparently have no school lessons, they seem free to just drift around, playing games, pursuing crushes, quarrels and intrigues, until it all turns sour. But there is a curious kind of acceptance; has Mari become institutionalised, just as the head teacher predicted, when she brought Mari back from the police station? A strange, bittersweet vignette.
points: With handheld camerawork, this unsentimental rite of passage film follows Mari, who tries to escape from a residential home in Estonia.

articles.title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85
articles.summary: Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile. Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The…
body: Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”

Born in Chile in 1941, Guzmán initially worked in advertising before studying film, first in Chile and then in Madrid. On his return to Chile, Guzmán responded to the febrile political atmosphere after Allende’s election in 1970, eventually completing the mammoth Battle of Chile documentary that chronicled Pinochet’s ultimately successful attempt to overthrow Allende, resulting in the latter’s suicide. Guzmán did not shrink from the brutality of the period, even including footage shot by camera operator Leonardo Henrichsen as he is shot dead by the soldier he is filming.
points: Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile.

articles.title: ‘Closing Night’ Review: Sarah Paulson and Naomi Watts Are Warring Sisters in Cody Fern’s Deliciously Histrionic Melodrama
articles.summary: Toward the end of the deep-feeling, deliciously histrionic drama “Closing Night,” the film shifts tone. The first two acts — a whirlwind of long-deferred confrontations and fiery disclosures — lean on lively dark comedy as a pair of warring sisters explode with decades of rage and resentment.
body: The powerhouse actresses play fragile women navigating a devastating diagnosis in this darkly comic story about the secrets that bind us.

When the film begins, Sandra has extended an olive branch to April and Diane by inviting them to New York to see her perform on Broadway. Diane refuses, but April hesitantly makes the trip, only to learn that Theo — an artistic dilettante who lives in the city with his girlfriend, Lucy (Odessa A’zion) — has been lunching with Sandra behind her back. April receives the news as a betrayal. But Theo, long kept in the dark about his mom and aunt’s rupture, sees the meetings as a chance to get to know the famous relative who was, until then, a stranger.

articles.title: In-I in Motion review – Juliette Binoche pulls back the curtain on dance duet with Akram Khan
articles.summary: The actor makes her directing debut with a raw, fascinating film about her 2008 collaboration with the British dancer. In the way that wedding rehearsals can be more emotional than the big day – all the untidy feelings that will be tucked away for the cameras still on show – this documentary from…
body: In-I in Motion is a film of two halves, ending with a performance on stage in front of an audience, the set designed by artist Anish Kapoor: a vast screen in murderous red. The first half is more interesting, shot fly-on-the-wall style during the months it took to create the piece in a studio. Binoche and Khan work with acting coach Susan Batson, who at one point thunders: “THIS IS FULL OF SHIT!” (never mind La Binoche’s Oscar). For some audiences, it will have a whiff of theatrical cringe; the endless stewing and fretting over how to achieve something truthful is ripe for spoof. But the pure intensity and focus is thrilling to watch.

articles.title: Your mission, Tom Cruise, is to improve at interviews. And please keep sending the cakes
articles.summary: He risks his life for entertainment, but getting an anecdote out of him is a trickier matter. Happily, Cruise is no stranger to knuckling down and pulling off the impossible. By now, we’ve grown used to watching Tom Cruise excel at everything he does. Running in films? The best.
body: But nobody is perfect. Live long enough and a few flaws will worm their way to the surface. This is as true for Tom Cruise as it is for anyone else. And while I realise that this might do me out of a cake this Christmas, the following really needs to be said: Tom Cruise isn’t very good at interviews.

As you will be aware, Cruise’s new film Digger comes out soon. The film is a risk. It is his first original, non-sequel, non-action film in which he co-stars since 2007’s Lions for Lambs. It is also, if the trailers are any indication, palpably batshit. This means that Cruise has to reintroduce himself to the world as an actor, rather than the guy who just flings himself off a variety of increasingly berserk surfaces. And this means promotion. Until this week, that promotion has involved either World Cup-themed promos filmed in character or interviews where the subject matter was almost exclusively limited to lens choice.
points: He risks his life for entertainment, but getting an anecdote out of him is a trickier matter.
Happily, Cruise is no stranger to knuckling down and pulling off the impossible.

articles.title: Tom Petty’s Original Heartbreakers to Reunite for First Time in Decades for Americana Awards, Fronted by Chris Stapleton; Boxed Set of ’70s Rarities Coming
articles.summary: It’s almost enough to un-break your heart, if you’re a Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers fan. The four members of the original/classic lineup of Petty’s longtime band will reunite on stage for the first time in more than 20 years this week, fronted by Chris Stapleton for an opening performance at…
body: Heartbreakers fans don’t have to experience too much FOMO about missing the on-stage reunion: The Americana Awards will be streamed live via video and audio through several outlets, beginning at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 PT. It can be seen on NPR Music’s YouTube channel and the Americana Music Association ‘s Facebook page; the audio feed can be found on SiriusXM’s Outlaw Country channel and clear-channel WSM-AM as well as Nashville’s FM stations WRLT and WMOT.

Campbell and Tench were lifers in Petty’s band until the frontman’s 2017 death. Bassist Ron Blair quit the Heartbreakers in 1982, but rejoined 20 years later. Drummer Stan Lynch left the group for good in 1994, seemingly with some musical estrangement from Petty at the time, though he was known to stay in loving contact with other members of the band in subsequent decades. Those four players did subsequently reunite with Petty on stage as a unit once after Lynch’s departure, playing two songs at their Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction in 2002.
points: It’s almost enough to un-break your heart, if you’re a Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers fan.

articles.title: Legendary Nigerian actor Olu Jacobs dies aged 84
articles.summary: Olu Jacobs was one of Nigeria's most recognised actors, whose career spanned several decades.
body: His wife, veteran actress Joke Silva, announced his death and asked for privacy while the family mourns.
Silva announced his passing in a statement describing the celebrated actor as "The Lion of Lufodo" and saying his life was "well lived and fought".
Some of his notable films include My Kingdom, Covert Operation and One Fine Day.
He was regarded as one of the father figures of Nollywood, as Nigeria's film industry in known, commanding widespread respect and admiration across the country.

articles.title: Earl Spencer's unreleased book on Diana stolen in the Netherlands
articles.summary: The theft of Earl Spencer's memoir about his late sister comes one week ahead of the book's release.
body: Copies of Earl Spencer's unreleased book on his sister Diana, Princess of Wales, have been stolen from a truck in the Netherlands.
The BBC understands four copies of the Dutch language edition were taken from a truck while it was en route from the Dutch publisher's printers to their warehouse.
Dutch police said they were aware of the incident and have been approached for comment.
Swan Song: Diana, My Sister is due to be released in the UK and globally on Tuesday, and tells the story of Princess Diana's life from the Earl's perspective.

articles.title: Writer and broadcaster Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
articles.summary: Her husband says the playwright and cultural and political commentator died after a brief illness.
body: British-American author and cultural commentator Bonnie Greer has died at the age of 77 after a brief illness, her husband has said.

In a statement delivered with "profound sadness", Greer's widower David Hutchins noted how the acclaimed playwright and critic had made "an enduring contribution to British cultural and public life" with her "intelligence, courage and distinctive voice".
He added: "To me, she was my partner, confidante and inspiration, and I feel profoundly privileged to have shared my life with her."
Hutchins continued: "Those closest to Bonnie will remember her warmth, humour, generosity and extraordinary ability to bring people together."
points: Her husband says the playwright and cultural and political commentator died after a brief illness.
